sovereign_country.strategic_role: 西欧核心消费市场、高客单价品牌合规与本土清关

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Cross-Border E-Commerce Overseas Warehouse Order Fulfillment

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: France (unitary national jurisdiction; no sub-state tax distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Romano-Germanic legal family; codified statutes prevail over judicial precedent)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Agreement between the Government of the French Republic and the Government of the People's Republic of China on the Reciprocal Encouragement and Protection of Investments (1984, as amended by exchange of notes in 2007)

Convention between the French Republic and the People's Republic of China for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with Respect to Taxes on Income and Capital (2013, in force 1 January 2015)
The Hague Convention of 5 October 1961 Abolishing the Requirement of Legalisation for Foreign Public Documents (Apostille Convention)
EU Common Commercial Policy instruments and EU external trade agreements attributable to France as a Member State

France-Singapore Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (1975) and France-Japan Double Taxation Avoidance Convention (2007) as supplementary counterparty-jurisdiction treaty references for the cross-border logistics route network

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Code monétaire et financier (CMF), Articles L.561-1 to L.561-57 and R.561-1 et seq. (customer due diligence, beneficial owner identification and TRACFIN reporting obligations); Article L.561-2-1 CMF (definition of beneficial owner); Ordinance No. 2016-1635 of 1 December 2016 and its implementing decrees (French AML/CFT enforcement framework); Decree No. 2020-118 of 12 February 2020 (transposition of Directive (EU) 2015/849 into French law); Code de commerce, Articles L.123-1-1, R.123-1 et seq. and Article 1835 of the Code civil (mandatory beneficial owner declaration filed with the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés and centralized in the Registre National des Entreprises); Decree No. 2023-1394 of 30 December 2023 (digital consolidation of the UBO register in the RNE).
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (general public access restricted following the Court of Justice of the European Union judgment of 22 November 2022, Case C-37/20; full access granted to TRACFIN, competent authorities, judicial authorities and obliged entities discharging statutory customer due diligence obligations through the RNE/Greffe secure channel)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the valid passport of each ultimate beneficial owner (natural person)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport-issuing authority of the UBO's country of nationality (e.g., National Immigration Administration of the People's Republic of China)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the competent origin-country authority where the origin country is party to the Apostille Convention; failing that, Consular Legalization by the competent French consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney (Pouvoir) in favor of the signatory of the articles of association (statuts)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public duly licensed in the shareholder's jurisdiction of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization as applicable, followed by sworn French translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent corporate register extract of each corporate shareholder and of each corporate UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry of the corporate shareholder's country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization as applicable, followed by sworn French translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of registered address of each shareholder and corporate UBO (utility invoice or bank statement issued within the preceding three months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or deposit-taking bank in the address jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization as applicable, followed by sworn French translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Source-of-funds bank reference letter and account verification statement for the equity contribution to be made to the SAS share capital
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home or relationship bank of the contributing shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization as applicable, followed by sworn French translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified French translation (traduction assermentée) of every foreign-language document in the apostilled bundle
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Certified translator enrolled with a French Cour d'appel (traducteur agréé près la Cour d'appel)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Attestation by the sworn translator; preconditioned on the underlying documents having received Apostille or Consular Legalization in their origin jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Compulsory pre-filing screening of each shareholder, UBO, director and statutory signatory against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List and the guidance of the French National Council for Financial Sanctions (Conseil national des sanctions financières, CNSF); mandatory politically exposed person (PEP) assessment consistent with FATF Recommendation 12 and Article L.561-10 of the Code monétaire et financier; enhanced due diligence triggered by PEP status, high-risk third-country links or unusual source-of-funds patterns; unconditional obligation to report suspicious or inconsistent facts to TRACFIN pursuant to Article L.561-15 CMF; the diligence is performed at pre-incorporation on the proposed statutory capacity and thereafter on a continuous monitoring basis.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) and the Registre National des Entreprises (RNE) accessible via data.inpi.fr; name availability is further verified against the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) maintained by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The articles of association must be executed in the French language; the corporate name may incorporate foreign or transliterated elements only to the extent they are rendered in Latin script and comply with public order; the name must not be deceptive as to the corporate form, must be distinct from earlier RCS-registered and trademark-protected names, and must incorporate the legal-form identifier 'SAS' or the full expression 'Société par Actions Simplifiée' in all formal correspondence; a foreign-language version of the name has no legal effect over the French statutory denomination
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: France / République / National (prior ministerial or state authorization required)
Commission / Autorité (regulatory-connoting tokens reserved for public authorities)
Any token implying governmental sponsorship, diplomatic status or public-sanctioned activity
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France applies a filing-based attribution rather than a statutory reservation system: the chosen name is examined at the moment the formation dossier is lodged through the Guichet Unique. Upon rejection, the Greffier or the RNE must issue a reasoned refusal; the applicant may cure the refusal by amending the requested name and re-submitting through the same portal without loss of the pre-incorporation file; an administrative reconsideration request must be addressed in writing within 15 days of the reasoned refusal to the issuing Greffier or to the INPI Director where the objection rests on an INPI trademark conflict; where the conflict stems from an opposed prior registration, an opposition must be lodged with the INPI within 30 days of publication or notification; judicial recourse lies to the competent Tribunal de Commerce or Tribunal judiciaire within two months of the final administrative refusal; in parallel, the applicant may preserve priority by filing an INPI trademark application for the corporate name under trademark law.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for the legal registered seat only through a licensed domiciliation company (société de domiciliation) in accordance with Article L.123-11-2 of the Code de commerce, provided the domiciliation agreement is evidenced at filing; however, for an ISIC 5210 cross-border e-commerce cross-dock order-fulfillment hub, operational substance must be established through a physically leased warehouse in France and the registered office must remain a genuine, permanently reachable address for service of process and customs correspondence; a purely virtual seat without any physical logistics footprint would impair both customs authorization and ordinary commercial credibility
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: HIGH for customs control context — approximately 60% probability of at least one unannounced physical inspection by the French Customs administration (Direction générale des douanes et droits indirects) or the DGCCRF consumer-protection authority within the first 12 months of operations, arising from the statutory right of inspection conferred by Article 64 of the French Customs Code over premises handling imported or re-exported merchandise; the likelihood rises to approximately 80% if the site operates under a customs suspension arrangement, holds bonded status, or processes goods destined to multiple EU member states; pre-incorporation documentary conformity and compliant UBO records materially reduce penalty exposure during such inspections

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark with statutory format requirements

UBO declaration compilation and RNE/UBO register filing preparation (beneficial ownership schedule, ownership chain chart and supporting evidence pack)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark and statutory administrative fee component

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff for notarial acts plus prevailing market benchmark for apostille processing

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified sworn French translations (traductions assermentées) of all foreign-language UBO, shareholder and source-of-funds documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Certified translator registered with a French Cour d'appel

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered-office domiciliation agreement (legal seat) for the first fiscal year through a licensed domiciliation company
Foreign shareholder KYC documentation and pre-operational bank account opening package (including Airwallex or French correspondent account setup)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark and bank tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PEP, OFAC, UN and EU consolidated sanctions screening solution with continuous monitoring for 12 months
EORI (Economic Operator Registration and Identification) registration with French Customs for cross-border customs operations
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Direction générale des douanes et droits indirects
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory — free of charge, mandatory for customs transactions

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation professional fee contingency reserve for supplementary apostille requests, additional sworn translations or regulatory clarifications
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Law firm / notary / corporate service provider, as applicable

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), including Articles L. 227-1 to L. 227-20 for the société par actions simplifiée (SAS), Articles L. 123-1 et seq. for the Trade and Companies Register (RCS), and Articles L. 561-46 et seq. of the Monetary and Financial Code for beneficial-owner reporting.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: The competent local Trade and Companies Registry (Registre du commerce et des sociétés, RCS), maintained by the clerk's office (greffe) of the territorially competent commercial court; filings are submitted through the national business formalities portal operated by INPI.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Electronic company-formation filing through the Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises, including the signed SAS articles of association (statuts), required declarations, and beneficial-owner filing.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital applies to an SAS. For cash contributions, at least 50% of subscribed shares must be paid at incorporation; the balance must be paid within five years of registration. Cash must be deposited with an authorized depositary, and a deposit certificate is included in the filing. Deposited funds are generally released to the company after registration. In-kind contributions are fully contributed at formation and may require a contribution auditor unless a statutory exemption applies.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTIONS OF THE PRESIDENT OF [COMPANY NAME] SAS. The President acknowledges the subscriptions set out in the executed articles of association and confirms that the required initial cash contributions have been deposited and certified. The Company adopts as its registered office the address stated in the articles of association, effective upon registration. [NAME] is appointed President for the term and on the terms specified in the articles of association. [NAME], if applicable, is appointed Directeur Général on those terms. The President is authorized to complete registration, beneficial-owner declarations, bank formalities, and all related filings, and to take actions necessary to commence the Company's stated business, subject to applicable permits.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Set corporate terms and prepare the SAS articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company promoters; advice from French counsel or a chartered accountant where appropriate
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Select the company name, registered office, duration, corporate purpose, share capital, share classes, governance rules, President, and any Directeur Général. Draft and execute the articles of association. Obtain any required authority for use of the registered-office address. Non-French-language supporting documents may require a French translation by a sworn translator; notarization or apostille is required only where applicable to the particular foreign document.
required_dossiers: Identity and address details for shareholders and officers
Registered-office occupancy evidence or domiciliation agreement
Any applicable powers of attorney and legalized or translated foreign documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct inconsistencies in the articles or supporting evidence, obtain missing signatures or translations, and re-execute amended documents before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized bank, notary, or other legally authorized depositary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a formation deposit account, transfer the cash contributions required to be paid at incorporation, and obtain the depositary's certificate. Ensure the subscription schedule and deposited amount reconcile. Obtain evidence of any in-kind contributions and determine whether a contribution auditor is required.
required_dossiers: Executed articles or draft articles accepted by the depositary
Proof of source of funds where requested
In-kind contribution report or exemption documentation, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Resolve identity, source-of-funds, or subscription discrepancies with the depositary; correct the subscription schedule and obtain a replacement certificate before the registry filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized legal-notice publication service (service de presse en ligne habilité or journal d'annonces légales) in the registered-office department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Publish the mandatory formation notice containing the prescribed company particulars and obtain the publication certificate. Use the company name, legal form, capital, registered office, purpose, term, and registry jurisdiction exactly as stated in the articles.
required_dossiers: Company particulars from the executed articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request correction or republication if prescribed particulars are missing or inconsistent; upload the corrected certificate with the filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI-operated Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises; routed to the competent local RCS clerk's office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Create the electronic formation filing, complete the required company, officer, establishment, and beneficial-owner information, upload the supporting documents, and pay the displayed fees. Disclose each reportable beneficial owner under applicable French rules. Retain the electronic acknowledgment and respond through the portal to any registry request.
required_dossiers: Officer identity, address, and non-disqualification declarations
Required identity documents and powers of attorney
Any required auditor appointment or contribution-auditor documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Use the portal's query or correction function to supply missing or corrected documents within the stated deadline, pay any additional fee, and request review by the competent RCS clerk if the rejection appears procedural or erroneous.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique, INSEE, the competent RCS, and the company's depositary bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the company identification number and Kbis extract, verify the registered particulars, and provide the Kbis to the depositary to release the capital. Complete tax, payroll, social-security, accounting, and invoicing registrations as applicable. Maintain statutory registers and record corporate decisions in accordance with the articles and French law.
required_dossiers: Kbis extract and company identification numbers
Employment and social-security information, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request correction of inaccurate register data through the Guichet unique or competent RCS; provide additional bank compliance documents and complete any outstanding tax or social-security registrations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No general industrial licensing board applies to ordinary cross-border warehousing and order-fulfilment operations. The competent local prefecture and its environmental services, generally the DREAL, oversee any applicable classified-facility requirements under the ICPE regime.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No general operating or manufacturing permit is ordinarily required solely for standard warehousing and fulfilment. A site may require an ICPE declaration, registration, or environmental authorization depending on stored materials, quantities, activities, and applicable nomenclature thresholds.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry for Ecological Transition (Ministère de la Transition écologique), with technical review commonly involving the Regional Directorate for Environment, Planning and Housing (DREAL) and environmental assessment authority as applicable
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Site- and activity-specific. An ICPE project may be subject to case-by-case environmental examination, an environmental impact assessment, or no EIA, depending on statutory thresholds and screening. Check applicable ICPE nomenclature, including warehouse and stored-material categories, before site fit-out or operation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Comply with any applicable ICPE order, prefectural permit conditions, water-law requirements, municipal sewer-discharge authorization, waste-traceability rules, and hazardous-material storage and fire-prevention requirements. No single wastewater or VOC threshold applies to all warehouses; limits depend on the activity, site authorization, receiving network, and applicable national or local rules.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Before opening, confirm building-use and planning compliance, fire-safety measures, emergency access, and any required building or fire-authority inspections. A warehouse open to employees must comply with the Labour Code, including risk assessment and a written occupational risk assessment document (DUERP). Structural load capacity must be verified for the intended racking and stored loads; applicable building, fire, and workplace approvals depend on the facility's use and classification.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) — impots.gouv.fr; dedicated 'Service des Impôts des Entreprises Étrangères' (SIEE) for non-established foreign corporations, together with the customs authority DGDDI for import/export VAT suspension regimes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign corporation must file the SIEE registration application (Cerfa number under the 'Demande d'immatriculation au service des impôts des entreprises étrangères' form), accompanied by the foreign VAT/TIN certificate, articles of incorporation, proof of the appointed French tax representative (régime de représentant fiscal) if not established in the EU, and a description of French taxable activities. DGFiP processes the file and issues a French SIREN/SIRET number and a French VAT number (FR + check digits); registration is mandatory before first taxable transaction unless a reverse charge or OSS/IOSS applies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (SAS is always subject to corporate income tax — no pass-through eligibility or partnership election).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box regime; possible election for tax consolidation (intégration fiscale) under CGI Art. 223 A where an SAS holds 95%+ of French subsidiaries; hybrid mismatch and anti-reverse-hybrid rules (ATAD) apply under CGI Art. 209/212, with no elective pass-through mechanism for an SAS.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (TVA — Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: French-established businesses: mandatory registration when taxable turnover exceeds EUR 85,000 for supplies of goods and EUR 37,500 for supplies of services under the 'franchise en base' exemption; non-established foreign businesses have a EUR 0 threshold and must register for French VAT before any taxable supply in France, unless reverse-charge or OSS/IOSS interim rules apply.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory e-invoicing and e-reporting will be phased in from 1 September 2026 (reception for all taxable persons; issuance for large and mid-size businesses) and 1 September 2027 (issuance by SMEs/micro-enterprises). Invoices must be transmitted through certified dematerialisation platforms (PDP/OD) via API in structured Factur-X/UBL formats, and transaction data must be reported to DGFiP's 'Annuaire' and AIF concentration hub. There is no prior fiscal stamping/real-time clearance requirement; compliance is enforced via audit trails.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For goods, zero-rating applies under CGI Art. 262-II (and EU VAT Directive Art. 146) when goods are physically dispatched/transported to a third country or intra-EU recipient, with proof of departure; for services, zero-rating applies where the B2B customer belongs outside the EU, resulting in a place of supply outside France; logistics and cross-dock services physically performed in France for foreign B2C customers may remain subject to French VAT if the place of supply is in France.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DAU, including ENS route and customs exit confirmation)
Bill of Lading / airway bill / CMR duly stamped by French or EU customs as having left the EU
Inward Remittance Certificate (SWIFT/MT103 or bank credit advice evidencing payment from the foreign buyer or acquirer) to substantiate FX repatriation.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The exporter must substantiate the physical exit and receipt of consideration; if proof is deficient, DGFiP will claw back the zero-rating, reassess French VAT on the taxed amount, and charge late-payment interest; deliberate misstatements attract a 40% penalty and organised fraud/misrepresentation an 80% penalty; customs fraud may separately trigger fines up to the value of the goods and criminal sanctions.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France, under the coordination of the French Ministry for the Economy, Finance and Industrial and Digital Sovereignty; prudential and AML/CFT supervision of banks and payment/e-money institutions is exercised by the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible; France does not operate exchange controls, dual exchange rates, transaction licences, or prior central-bank approvals on current-account or capital-account movements between France and other EU/EEA states. Capital flows between France and non-EU jurisdictions are equally liberalized, subject to EU financial sanctions and French foreign-investment screening rules for specifically defined sensitive sectors. Profit remittances by a French SAS (dividends, branch profits, interest and royalties) are not blocked by FX law; the only real hurdles are source-country withholding taxes (e.g., 25% or treaty-reduced on non-EU dividends) and documentary substantiation for the paying bank. A French SAS may hold foreign-currency accounts domestically and, subject to annual tax disclosure, maintain bank accounts abroad. Every qualifying cross-border wire transfer above the applicable surveillance threshold is systematically recorded by the intermediary and reported to Banque de France for balance-of-payments statistics; practical approval is therefore a bank-compliance matter rather than a central-bank matter.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France imposes no statutory repatriation timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no surrender obligation on export proceeds. Since full liberalization of the French exchange-control regime, exporters, freight forwarders, and 3PL logistics operators are free to keep their foreign-currency receivables abroad or in French foreign-currency accounts without any euro conversion obligation. The residual duty is statistical: French credit institutions must report to Banque de France all cross-border monetary transactions above the applicable threshold, and French companies may in addition be required to answer Banque de France balance-of-payments surveys. For an overseas warehouse / cross-dock fulfilment company, the underlying export documentation (invoices, customs declarations, warehouse contracts, order-fulfilment reports) must be retained to support each cross-border receipt if the bank is asked to justify a transaction.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (compte bloqué) for pre-incorporation share capital deposit; Operational EUR/USD/GBP account after KBIS registration
Operational multi-currency account with cash management; capital escrow support for SAS incorporation
Operational current account; French SEPA IBAN; treasury and trade finance desk
Operational current account; import/export documentary services
Professional operational account for SME logistics entities

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility for EU/EEA-licensed electronic money institutions and payment institutions that passport into France under PSD2, notably Airwallex, Qonto, Wise Business, and Revolut Business. These fintechs provide fast API-driven cross-border payouts, foreign-currency merchant settlement, and multi-currency IBAN collection solutions at materially lower cost than Tier-1 incumbent banks. Legal constraints appear for 'offshore' EMIs located outside the EU/EEA: a Singapore, Hong Kong, or UK-only EMI cannot independently hold a French clearing account or maintain a genuine French payment account unless it obtains an EU/EEA licence, passports into France, or operates through an ACPR-authorized agent. Recommended structure: use Airwallex or Qonto for operational payment rails and payout automation, and maintain one Tier-1 French bank account for capital-escrow duties, documentary LC/collections, and contingency liquidity.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no general statutory mandate requiring directors to appear physically before a French bank; French AML/KYC law permits remote identification using ACPR-recognised video-identification and electronic-signature procedures. In practice, however, BNP Paribas, Société Générale, and most Tier-1 relationship banks request at least one in-person meeting when the legal representative or any UBO is non-resident, especially when the corporate chain is cross-border. Remote onboarding is commonly accepted by fintech and neobank platforms. For the French SAS structure, we recommend sending the actual signatory (or a duly appointed local authorized representative) to a relationship-banking meeting in France if Tier-1 bank services are desired; simultaneously maintain an API-accessible EMI account to preserve operational agility.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-EU parent / fast-moving cross-border group with an opacity issue in the ultimate beneficial ownership (UBO) chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Updated French RBE (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs) extract; statutory share register and shareholders’ agreement of the French SAS; certified corporate extract and UBO declaration for each intermediate holding company; passport copies of all natural-person UBOs; signed organisational chart; apostille/consular legalization of foreign corporate documents; written explanation of the commercial rationale for the ownership chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity e-commerce fulfilment cash flows presenting characteristics of payments aggregation, commingled cargo, or inadequate underlying trade documentation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed warehouse-binding and order-fulfilment contracts with each e-commerce platform/seller; customs records and customs-broker instructions; invoices for storage, pick-and-pack, freight forwarding and cross-dock handling; periodic inventory and shipment movement reports; seller onboarding policies; customer due-diligence files; internal AML risk assessment showing the account is not used as an unlicensed money-service business.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds concern with regard to the initial capital injection from an offshore holding entity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statements of the remitting entity covering the relevant period; SWIFT/SEPA payment instruction showing purpose code EQUI or INTC; share-subscription resolution and share issue agreement; notary or statutory incorporation certificate; confirmation of no non-resident capital controls in the remitting jurisdiction; if applicable, direct-investment statistical declaration submitted to Banque de France; audited or management accounts of the parent to evidence available funds and legitimate source.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and jurisdiction risk arising from counterparties in high-risk or restricted countries linked to e-commerce fulfilment channels
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Documented sanctions-screening policy with automated KYB/KYC tool outputs; restricted-party and consolidated screening results; list of approved shipping origin/destination countries; contractual embargo and export-control clauses; refusal logs for rejected counterparties; independent country-risk assessment; senior management AML attestation; periodic EDD refresh for any high-risk counterparty retained under an enhanced due-diligence rationale.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For pre-incorporation capital, open a temporary French bank account in the name of the 'SAS en formation' and instruct the parent to transfer funds via normal international banking channels. For inbound EUR from EEA, a SEPA Credit Transfer is sufficient; for non-EEA inbound, use SWIFT MT103 with the receiving French bank's BIC and the SAS's IBAN. Use ISO 20022 purpose code EQUI (Equity Investment) for share capital or INTC (Intercompany Payment) for shareholder loans, and place a clear narrative in Field 70: 'Capital subscription - SAS [Name] - transformation of French entity'. The bank will normally request a signed subscription deed, the draft legal status (statuts), UBO list, and a statement of no proceeds from suspicious sources. After the Kbis is issued, funds are released to the operational account. All inbound transfers above the regulatory reporting threshold are automatically captured in Banque de France balance-of-payments statistics; no prior central-bank approval is required for this non-sensitive 3PL activity, but the bank will verify the transaction against the foreign-investment-screen (I 151-3 CMF) only if the investor falls into a sensitive sector or is a foreign state entity.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SWIFT MT103 for high-frequency supplier payments, freight charges, customs payments, and disbursements to overseas warehouse operators; use SEPA Credit Transfer for euro payments to EEA beneficiaries. For larger or contractually risky procurement of cross-border inventory, an irrevocable commercial Letter of Credit (SWIFT MT700) or documentary collection (D/P or D/A) settled through the French bank is permitted and recommended. SWIFT GPI tracking should be enabled for end-to-end visibility. Each outward payment should name the underlying invoice, contract number, and customs reference; payment instructions must contain the beneficiary's full legal name, IBAN/account, and BIC. All transactions above the surveillance threshold are included in the bank's periodic reporting to Banque de France and must be supported by commercial documents retained for at least five years.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable EUR/USD FX forward (change à terme) with an ACPR-licensed French or EU bank to hedge USD-denominated customer settlements and supplier invoices
FX swap (change swap) for short-tenor matching of USD receipts with EUR payables or vice versa
Plain-vanilla European FX options to hedge forecast but not yet contracted cross-border cash flows
Cross-currency swap only where a currency-denominated financing or intercompany loan exists and the hedge is genuine and proportionate

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are permissible only when executed with an EU/EEA-authorized investment firm or bank, subject to EMIR margin/clearing eligibility and the customer being treated as a professional counterparty; NDFs may be used for hedging non-convertible or illiquid emerging-market currency exposures in relevant supplier channels

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual shareholder decision approving annual accounts and appropriation of result (AGM / décision de l'associé unique)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: SAS shareholder or sole shareholder; recorded in Registre des décisions (Minute Book); no external filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months of fiscal year-end; calendar-year SAS by 30 June, unless extended by court order
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene or approve prevents timely filing of accounts, exposes management to civil liability, and with repeated RCS non-compliance may trigger administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements and annexes deposit (dépôt des comptes annuels)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (RCS) via formalités.entreprises.gouv.fr / INPI
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after shareholder approval; for calendar-year SAS no later than 31 July unless extended
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or non-filing is subject to court-ordered compliance and fines up to EUR 7,500; persistent failure may result in administrative strike-off from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (liasse fiscale: form 2065-SD and schedules 2050-series)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGFiP – Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE) via EDI TDFC
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar-year SAS: e-file by 3 May of the following year; non-calendar fiscal year: within three months after fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or incomplete filing triggers late-payment interest, a 5% late filing margin, and separate penalties of 40% or 80% for undisclosed items; wilful omissions may also attract criminal tax penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory audit report and auditor appointment confirmation (if audit thresholds are exceeded or bylaws require)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders at the ordinary meeting; auditor details recorded in the RCS file when appointed; report accompanies annual accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Auditor report must be issued before the AGM; accounts approved within six months of year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to obtain a required auditor opinion may render the accounts non-regular and block RCS deposit; court may appoint an auditor and directors may face civil and criminal liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual social declaration and payroll reconciliation (Déclaration Sociale Nominative and annual URSSAF reconciliation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly DSN by the 5th or 15th of the following month depending on employer size; annual reconciliation and social data certification due by 31 January of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or missing declarations produce fixed per-employee penalties, administrative fines, loss of social attestation, and possible director liability for unpaid social charges.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual local business property tax contribution (Cotisation Foncière des Entreprises) payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGFiP – Service des Impôts des Entreprises / local public finance office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Payment of the assessed CFE notice by 15 December; initial declaration within 3 months of commencement; changes reported before the end of the tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-payment applies a 10% increase plus monthly interest, enforced recovery, and potential corporate liability; it does not itself trigger administrative strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An SAS must appoint a statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) if it exceeds at least two of three thresholds at fiscal year-end: balance-sheet total EUR 4,000,000; net turnover excluding VAT EUR 8,000,000; average headcount of 50. Audit is also mandatory where required by the articles, shareholder request, or group consolidation rules.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Individual statutory accounts are prepared under French GAAP (règlement ANC 2014-03 / Plan Comptable Général); consolidated accounts, if required, are prepared under EU-endorsed IFRS or French GAAP as applicable.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: French law does not require a standalone annual UBO confirmation return. The beneficial-owner declaration is filed with the RCS within 15 days after any change in beneficial ownership or control, including share transfers. Each share transfer must be recorded in the Registre des mouvements de titres and authenticated by the SAS president. The annual secretarial review verifies the UBO record and share-transfer register before the AGM and before depositing annual accounts.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members and Share Transfers (Registre des mouvements de titres)
Register of Decisions and Minute Book (Registre des décisions de l'associé)
Register of Directors and Corporate Officers (Registre des mandataires sociaux)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 – 25,000 for a full annual statutory audit of a cross-dock/3PL SAS, depending on headcount, revenue scope, and group consolidation requirements

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate for qualifying SMEs on first €42,500 of profit; R&D tax credit up to 30%; Innovation status tax rate of 15%

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 1200-A (Déclaration de résultat) via impots.gouv.fr professional space
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 3 months after the end of the fiscal year (e.g., by 31 March for calendar year 2023)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: N/A - French SAS is a tax resident

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Impôt sur les sociétés dû
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: N/A - French SAS is a tax resident

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: €125 per month of delay, maximum €7,500; plus late payment interest at 0.2% per month; possible criminal prosecution

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for EU/EEA parent companies under EU directive; 12.8% for non-EU recipients (treaty reduced)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Submit Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) and beneficial ownership form to French tax authorities through the impots.gouv.fr portal for DTA relief
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 0% intra-EU; 10-25% otherwise reduced by tax treaty; Interest: 0% intra-group or EU; 25% for third countries reduced by treaty

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: €50 million for local file; €750 million consolidated revenue for master file
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: French ESR applies to high-risk activities such as IP holding or financing; logistics and 3PL services generally do not trigger ESR unless specific conditions met

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Fraudulent under-declaration of income or overstatement of expenses to evade corporate tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Up to 5 years imprisonment and fines up to 80% of the evaded tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal criminal liability, possible imprisonment, and repayment of tax with surcharges

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Non-compliance with documentation requirements or use of non-arm's length pricing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines from €10,000 to €100,000 per infringement plus profit reassessment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability for directors who knowingly facilitated non-compliant TP arrangements

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to withhold and remit WHT on cross-border dividends, royalties, or interest
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty of 10% of the WHT amount due plus interest and possible criminal sanctions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal liability for the unpaid taxes and penalties
